target.title: improve(ios): show connection progress and errors prominently in onboarding gateway step
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Resolves a problem where users connecting to a gateway during iOS onboarding ("Gateway Details", step 2 of 4) could easily miss what was happening. Connection progress and failures were rendered as flat text rows ("Status", "Progress") plus a small footer caption — an error like "Gateway rejected the connection" appeared only as easy-to-overlook fine print, with no visible error state, no retry affordance, and no access to error details. ## Why This Change Was Made The connect step now derives an explicit connection phase (connecting / failed / ready) and renders it as the first, prominent element of the Status section: a spinner with the live target while connecting, the existing `GatewayProblemBanner` (icon, semantic tint, Retry/primary action, Details sheet) for typed `GatewayConnectionProblem` failures — the same treatment the Auth step already uses — and a danger `OpenClawNoticeBanner` with Retry for status-text-only failures. The redundant "Status"/"Progress" rows and the footer caption were removed. No new components; the banner, details sheet, and action handlers already existed at wizard level and are reused. ## User Impact During onboarding, users now clearly see whether the app is connecting, why a connection failed, and can retry or open error details directly on the Gateway Details screen instead of digging the failure reason out of fine print. ## Evidence Manually tested on a real iOS device (home-network onboarding). Before: the rejection only appeared as plain text in the "Status" row and a small caption below the section. After: the Status section leads with a prominent connection-state view (spinner + live detail while connecting, e.g. "Verifying gateway TLS fingerprint…"; error banner with Retry/Details on failure).
